conflict_topics: washing shared cookware immediately after use
giving a heads-up for late cooking
fair access to stove on weeknights
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants propose concrete, practical rules (wash-after-use, avoid strong smells/pork, give heads-up) rather than abstract principles.
C provides immediate action ("I'll wash the pan now") which helps settle the immediate problem.
Some redundant confirmations occur (D repeats adherence multiple times in Round 5).
Roles and factual points remain consistent (who cooks pork, who returned late) and are referenced in support of positions.
evaluation.final_reason: Housemates agreed to concrete rules and immediate actions. Key quoted lines: B proposed the rules: "Can we agree to wash shared cookware right after use and avoid strong-smell/pork cooking on weeknights?" C agreed and acted: "Agree... I'll wash the pan now." A earlier accepted practical steps: "Fine — I will open the window, switch the extractor, and give a heads-up if I cook late." D likewise accepted heads-up and wash-after-use. Together these constitute a mutual spoken agreement: everyone accepted wash-after-use, avoid strong smells/pork on weeknights, and give a quick heads-up when cooking late; C also washed the pan immediately.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially the target of complaint; defended not cooking pork but agreed to practical steps and the wash-after-use rule (Round 2: "Fine — I will open the window..."; Round 4: "We're agreed...").
Agent D: started by saying stove use on weeknights felt "impossible" but accepted wash-after-use and heads-up norms (Round 2 & 4: "I'll give a quick heads-up...").

Agent C: moved from pointing out the dirty pan to immediate remediation and constructive proposals (Round 1 & 3: "I'll wash the pan now... If you can't, tell us and wash before you go to bed; if this keeps happening we'll set a simple weekly rota.").
Agent B: consistently pushed for rules and immediate action; remained the instigator of the proposed norms but accepted the group's wording when others agreed.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B demands immediate changes and new rules: "Can you open the kitchen window and switch the extractor on? ... wash shared cookware right after use and avoid strong-smell/pork cooking on weeknights?" Agent A has not yet responded; C supports washing the pan but the core incompatibility (B's demand versus A's recent cooking) is unresolved.

D accepts the wash-after-use norm but requests fair chance to use the stove and proposes heads-up: "washing shared pans right after use is fair... just give a quick heads-up if someone needs to cook late." A concedes practical actions but pushes back on blame: "Fine — I will open the window... I don't cook pork, so that pan wasn't mine; everyone must wash shared cookware right after use." Tension about blame remains but substantive demands are largely accepted.

Group reaches explicit, mutual acceptance of the proposed rules. B asks for confirmation; C: "Agree... I'll wash the pan now." Combined with earlier acceptances (A and D), the household accepts: wash shared pans after use, avoid strong smells/pork on weeknights, and give a quick heads-up if cooking late.

Participants reaffirm and enact the agreement: D: "I'll give a quick heads-up..." A: "I'll open the window and switch the extractor on now. We're agreed: wash shared cookware right after use, avoid strong smells/pork on weeknights, and give a quick heads-up..." No substantive disagreement appears.
D repeatedly confirms adherence to the agreed rules: "I'll stick to wash-after-use and give a quick heads-up..." No new disagreement.
No public speech or observable action recorded; prior agreement stands and no new conflict appears.

substantive_insights: The conflict combined an immediate practical issue (unwashed pan with pork fat causing smell) with ongoing schedule/comfort concerns (B needs sleep; D returns late).
Resolution blended immediate remediation (C washed the pan, A opened window/extractor) with standing norms (wash-after-use, heads-up for late cooking) and a backup rota proposal.
Blame was a secondary tension; A defended not being the pork cook but still accepted procedural rules, which helped de-escalate the interpersonal element.
